cohort: 150 ASA class II patients undergoing elective caesarean sections under spinal anaesthesia, excluding those with a history of cerebrovascular or cardiovascular illness.
finding: The tilt posture provides improved stabilization of the heart rate, maintenance of blood pressure, and elevation of arterial pressure during caesarean delivery under spinal anaesthesia, potentially reducing hypotension and complications.
mod_finding: The study found that a 15-degree left lateral tilt during caesarean delivery under spinal anaesthesia significantly improved maternal haemodynamic responses, including heart rate stability, blood pressure maintenance, and elevated arterial pressure, compared to the supine position.
